cons: Not much energy return for faster days

name: Saucony Guide 19
description: The 2026 version of Saucony's long-running stability trainer, continuing the CenterPath guidance approach with PWRRUN+ foam on a broad, stable platform. It's built for overpronators and heel strikers who want structured daily mileage. Expect an evolution of the Guide 18 rather than a redesign.
cons: Modest update over the previous version

name: Saucony Hurricane 25
description: Saucony's premium max-cushion stability shoe, pairing a PWRRUN PB core with a firmer PWRRUN frame and CenterPath geometry for real guidance without a rigid post. It gives overpronators a plush, planted platform for daily and long miles. A strong pick for bigger runners who need both cushion and support.
cons: Feels ponderous at anything faster than easy pace

name: Saucony Hurricane 26
description: The 2026 Hurricane continues the formula of a soft PWRRUN PB core inside a supportive frame with CenterPath guidance. It's Saucony's flagship stability trainer for runners who want maximum cushion and structure in one shoe. Released mid-2026 as an incremental refinement of the Hurricane 25.
pros: Built to last under bigger runners
cons: One of the heavier trainers in the lineup

name: Saucony Kinvara 15
description: The long-running lightweight trainer that keeps things simple: PWRRUN foam, a 4mm drop, and very little else. It rewards efficient midfoot strikers who want a light, flexible shoe for daily miles and up-tempo days without plates or gimmicks. Minimal outsole rubber keeps weight down but limits durability.
pros: Good value for a lightweight trainer

name: Saucony Kinvara 17
description: The 2026 revival of Saucony's minimalist-leaning lightweight trainer, keeping the low 4mm drop and stripped-down build the line is known for. It suits efficient runners who want ground feel and a light platform for daily training and strides. Still one of the lightest unplated trainers you can buy.
cons: Not cushioned enough for long runs for most

name: Saucony Ride 18
description: Saucony's core neutral daily trainer, running a full PWRRUN+ TPU-bead midsole that is softer and bouncier than the old Ride formula. It handles easy miles, moderate long runs, and everyday training without drama. A safe, versatile first shoe for most runners.
pros: PWRRUN+ midsole is durable and lively
cons: Not fast enough for real workouts
Some rivals feel more exciting at this price

name: Saucony Ride 19
description: The 2026 update to Saucony's workhorse neutral trainer, keeping the PWRRUN+ midsole and balanced 8mm-drop platform with a refined upper. It stays true to the Ride formula: one shoe that covers most of a training week. Nothing flashy, just dependable daily mileage.
cons: Not a workout or race shoe

name: Saucony Tempus 2
description: A rare thing: a genuinely fast stability shoe. The Tempus 2 wraps a bouncy PWRRUN PB core in a supportive PWRRUN frame that guides the foot without a plate or a post. It lets overpronators pick up the pace in a shoe that still protects their stride, and plenty of neutral runners like it too.
pros: PEBA core gives real energy return
Works for neutral and overpronating runners alike
cons: Frame can feel firm underfoot at easy paces

name: Saucony Triumph 23
description: Saucony's premium max-cushion neutral trainer, notable for moving to a full PEBA-based PWRRUN PB midsole — race-shoe foam in a plush daily package. It delivers a soft, bouncy ride for long runs and recovery days while staying reasonably light for its stack. One of the more energetic plush trainers on the market.
pros: PEBA-based foam is soft and springy
cons: High 10mm drop won't suit forefoot strikers

name: Saucony Triumph 24
description: The newest Triumph keeps the full PWRRUN PB midsole that transformed the line and refines the upper and outsole. It remains Saucony's plushest neutral trainer, aimed at long runs, high mileage, and runners who want a soft but lively ride. Freshly released for mid-2026.
cons: Too soft and tall for fast workouts

name: Skechers Aero Burst
description: The cushioned pillar of Skechers' performance-focused Aero line, with a tall Hyper Burst Ice midsole for soft, high-mileage comfort. It targets easy days and long runs, undercutting most max-cushion competitors on price.
pros: Soft, high-stack cushioning at a value price

name: Skechers Aero Burst 2
description: The second edition of Skechers' max-cushion Aero trainer keeps the soft Hyper Burst Ice midsole and rockered shape with a refreshed upper. It remains an easy-day and long-run shoe that undercuts most max-cushion rivals on price.
pros: Plush cushioning at a value price

name: Skechers Aero Razor
description: The Razor name returns inside the Aero line as a light, unplated speed trainer built on Hyper Burst foam. Like past Razors it is a workout specialist that efficient runners can also use as a fast daily shoe.
pros: Continues the well-loved Razor speed-shoe lineage
Light, snappy ride without a plate
cons: Not cushioned enough for long easy miles

name: Skechers Aero Spark
description: The lightweight trainer of the Aero line, using Hyper Burst foam in a lower, nimbler package for uptempo daily running. It suits runners who want one affordable shoe for everyday miles, strides, and faster sessions.
pros: Light and lively for the price

name: Skechers Aero Spark 2
description: The 2026 follow-up to Skechers' lightweight Aero trainer keeps the low-slung Hyper Burst ride for uptempo daily miles with minor fit refinements. It stays one of the cheaper ways into a genuinely light performance trainer.
pros: Very light for a trainer at this price
Handles both easy and fast days
cons: Not enough shoe for high-mileage long runs

name: Skechers Aero Tempo
description: The plated speed shoe of the Aero line, combining Hyper Burst Ice foam with a stiffening plate for tempo runs and workouts. It plays the budget super-trainer role, giving plated pop well below the price of most competitors.
pros: Plated propulsion at a low price
cons: Less refined than premium super trainers
Fit runs a touch long for some

name: Skechers Aero Tempo 2
description: The second version of Skechers' plated tempo shoe carries forward the Hyper Burst Ice midsole and plate with a lighter upper. It remains a strong value pick for workouts and racing without paying super-shoe prices.
pros: Excellent price for a plated workout shoe
Versatile from tempo to race day
cons: Not as propulsive as top-tier carbon racers
Brand perception still lags its performance

name: Skechers GoRun Ride 12
description: Skechers' core neutral daily trainer with a full Hyper Burst supercritical midsole that delivers a soft yet lively ride at a fair price. It is one of the better value daily trainers on the market for easy miles and general training.
pros: Bouncy Hyper Burst foam at a modest price
cons: Outsole durability trails the big brands
Skechers still fights a lifestyle-brand image among runners

name: Topo Athletic Magnifly 5
description: Topo's zero-drop road trainer stacks 30mm of ZipFoam under the whole foot, giving natural-running fans real cushioning without an offset. With its anatomical toe box and flexible forefoot, it's a direct, more padded alternative to the Altra Escalante.
pros: Anatomical toe box with secure midfoot

name: Topo Athletic Specter 2
description: Topo's plateless super-trainer runs a full Pebax midsole under an anatomical wide toe box and a low 5mm drop. It's a bouncy, versatile shoe that handles daily miles and uptempo work for runners who want performance foam without a cramped racing fit.
pros: Roomy toe box on a performance shoe
cons: No plate means less snap than racers
Fit runs generous for narrow feet

name: Under Armour Infinite Elite
description: Under Armour's max-cushion flagship trainer with a thick HOVR+ supercritical midsole and a broad, stable platform. It is a plush cruiser for easy days and long runs, and its durable build suits bigger runners, though it carries noticeable weight.
pros: Stable base for a tall shoe
cons: Ride feels sluggish at faster paces

name: Under Armour Infinite Pro
description: The mid-tier shoe in UA's Infinite line, with HOVR+ foam in a more moderate stack than the Elite for balanced everyday training. It is a comfortable, well-built daily trainer that competes on cushioning and durability rather than low weight.
pros: Balanced HOVR+ cushioning for daily miles
cons: A bit heavy versus similarly priced rivals
Nothing about the ride stands out

name: Under Armour Velociti Elite 2
description: Under Armour's carbon-plated marathon racer, refining the shoe that carried Sharon Lokedi to a New York City Marathon win. It pairs a PEBA-based Flow midsole with a full carbon plate and UA's rubberless Flow outsole for a light, grippy, race-focused ride.
pros: Light with excellent road grip from the Flow outsole
cons: Super-shoe price from a challenger brand
